description: One pull request per repository for everything non-breaking, rather than one per dependency. Merging them singly means every merge rebases the others and restarts their checks: one run over an organisation of 34 repositories updated 109 branches and merged 2. Grouped, a repository needs one round of checks instead of dozens.

Never auto-merge the Go toolchain, and never let it ride in somebody else's group. A rule that says automerge:false for one dependency is defeated by grouping, because Renovate decides automerge per BRANCH: go 1.27.0 rode into seven repositories inside a branch called renovate/github-actions, whose other dependency was actions/setup-go. Ungrouped, it gets a branch of its own and this setting governs it. It matters because go1.27.0 miscompiles on loong64 (golang/go#81000, bisected on real hardware to 3fdac6780b): go-gfx/gfx fails that lane and stayed open only because the lane failed, which is the CI gate holding rather than this rule. A repository without such a lane sees nothing.

Hold the CI Python at 3.14 or below. It is not this port's own interpreter -- nothing here runs Python -- it is the one that has to run real ansible-core, the reference the conformance tests in inventory, template, vault and playbook measure against. ansible-core 2.21.4 INSTALLS cleanly on Python 3.15 and then refuses to start: ansible/module_utils/_internal/_patches/__init__.py patches CPython internals and reads dataclasses._is_type, a private attribute 3.15 removed, so the first ansible command dies with AttributeError: module 'dataclasses' has no attribute '_is_type' (measured 2026-10-18 on macos-latest, go-ansible/inventory#32).

The successful install is the trap: without a step that actually RUNS the interpreter, 3.15 looks fine and the oracle quietly stops being an oracle while every test still passes. The `ansible -m ping` smoke test added on 2026-10-18 is what turned it into a red job -- the CI gate holding, exactly as the Go toolchain rule above describes, rather than this file. Note that the first rule automerges minor updates, so a green run would have merged this one unattended. Raise the ceiling when ansible-core itself supports 3.15, and re-run that smoke test on macOS before believing it.
